items.title: Configuration reference
items.text:
Every setting Jocasta reads, with its type, default and the values it takes. Configure explains how settings are read and overridden. jocasta.example.yaml holds the same settings as a file to copy from.

Each setting can also come from an environment variable: JOCASTA_, then the setting's path in capitals with a double underscore between levels. A single underscore stays part of the key, so scan.devices.resolve_mdns is JOCASTA_SCAN__DEVICES__RESOLVE_MDNS. For a plugin or notification setting, the instance or destination name is one level of the path: plugins.routeros.gateway.password is JOCASTA_PLUGINS__ROUTEROS__GATEWAY__PASSWORD.

Types:

  • duration: a number and a unit, such as 90s, 15m or 6h. The units are s, m and h; there is no unit for days, so 30 days is 720h.
  • list: a YAML list.
  • map: YAML keys and values.

items.title: server
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description server.host string localhost An address or host name Where the web server listens. 0.0.0.0 listens on every interface. The container image sets 0.0.0.0. server.port int 8080 1 to 65535 The port the web server listens on. server.trusted_proxies list empty Addresses or CIDR prefixes, such as 192.0.2.1 or 10.0.0.0/8 Reverse proxy addresses whose forwarding headers the server trusts to identify the client. Empty reads the client address from the connection directly. server.cors.allowed_origins list empty Origins as scheme://host[:port] Browser origins besides the server's own that may read /api. Empty sends no CORS headers. server.auth.session_lifetime duration 168h A duration The longest a sign-in lasts, whatever the activity. server.auth.idle_timeout duration 24h A duration How long a session survives with no requests. server.auth.cookie_secure bool true true, false Sends the session cookie over HTTPS only. Set false to sign in over plain HTTP from anywhere but localhost. server.mcp.enabled bool false true, false Serves the MCP endpoint at /mcp. While off, /mcp answers 404.

items.title: db
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description db.path string . A directory Where the SQLite file lives. The container image sets /data. db.name string jocasta.db A file name The SQLite file's name.

items.title: logger
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description logger.level string info debug, info, warn, error The lowest level logged. Any other value logs at info. logger.format string json json, text How each log line is written. Any value but text writes JSON.

items.title: inventory
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description inventory.online_window duration 15m A duration How long after its last sighting a device counts as online. Past it, a watched device goes quiet. inventory.address_grace duration 6h A duration How long an address can go unseen before a later sweep that finds the device elsewhere retires it. Raise it on a network with long DHCP leases.

items.title: retention
items.text:
Records older than their window are deleted once an hour. 0s keeps that kind of record forever.

Key Type Default Allowed values Description retention.history duration 2160h (90 days) A duration; 0s keeps forever How long the change log and the scan log are kept. retention.traffic duration 720h (30 days) A duration; 0s keeps forever How long hourly traffic totals are kept. retention.dns duration 720h (30 days) A duration; 0s keeps forever How long hourly lookup counts, and the addresses lookups were answered with, are kept. retention.devices duration 2160h (90 days) A duration; 0s keeps forever How long a device nobody labelled, grouped, typed, noted or ignored is kept after a scan last saw it.

items.title: location
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description location.country string empty A two-letter country code, such as AU The country the world map draws its lines from. Empty uses the router's outside address, which cannot place a network behind carrier-grade NAT. See NetFlow. location.timezone string empty An IANA zone name, such as Australia/Sydney The zone times are shown in. Empty uses TZ or the system's zone, which is UTC in a container. Times are stored in UTC either way.

items.title: networks
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description networks list empty Prefixes, such as 192.0.2.0/24 The prefixes the sweep covers on a timer. Each address found is filed under the network that contains it.

items.title: scan
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description scan.source string sweep:<hostname> Any name The origin recorded for timed sweeps. Set it in a container, where the host name changes on every run. A new name starts a new source and leaves past scans under the old one. scan.devices.enabled bool true true, false Sweeps networks on a timer. scan.devices.interval duration 5m A duration How often the sweep runs. scan.devices.rate int 1000 A whole number The most ICMP probes sent per second. scan.devices.rounds int 2 A whole number Probes sent to each address before it counts as down. scan.devices.wait duration 2s A duration How long to wait for replies after the last probe. scan.devices.resolve_names bool true true, false Looks up reverse DNS for each address that answered. See Name devices. scan.devices.resolve_macs bool true true, false Reads the neighbour table for hardware addresses. scan.devices.resolve_mdns bool true true, false Asks each device without a reverse DNS name for its name over mDNS. scan.devices.resolve_netbios bool true true, false Asks each device still without a name over NetBIOS. scan.devices.resolve_dnssd bool true true, false Browses the services devices advertise, and names the rest after the name they give them. Needs host networking. scan.devices.resolve_ssdp bool true true, false Searches over SSDP, and names the rest after their UPnP friendlyName. Needs host networking. scan.ports.enabled bool false true, false Probes every known address for open TCP ports on a timer. scan.ports.interval duration 6h A duration How often the port scan runs. scan.ports.custom string empty Ports and ranges, such as 22,80,443,8000-8100; 1-65535 for every port The ports to probe. Empty uses a curated preset. Each address is also probed on the ports its device advertises. scan.ports.concurrency int 64 A whole number The most connections a scan opens at once. Lower it on a router with a small connection table.

items.title: notify
items.text:
Each destination sits under notify, keyed by a name you choose, and holds exactly one service block: ntfy, webhook or http. Which changes it is sent is picked on the account menu's Notifications page. See Notifications.

Key Type Default Allowed values Description notify.<name>.enabled bool true true, false Sends to this destination. A destination is on unless it says false. notify.<name>.timeout duration 10s A duration The longest one send may take.

items.title: ntfy
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description notify.<name>.ntfy.url string none, required The topic's URL, as ntfy shows it Where messages are published, such as https://ntfy.example.com/jocasta. notify.<name>.ntfy.token string empty An ntfy access token For a server that requires one. notify.<name>.ntfy.priority int 0 0 to 5 ntfy's priority, from 1 (min) to 5 (max). 0 leaves it to the server.

items.title: webhook
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description notify.<name>.webhook.url string none, required An HTTP or HTTPS URL Where the signed JSON POST goes. notify.<name>.webhook.secret string none, required Any Keys the signature on each request. See Check a webhook's signature.

items.title: http
items.text: Key Type Default Allowed values Description notify.<name>.http.url string none, required An HTTP or HTTPS URL Where the request goes. It can hold the service's token; it is never logged or shown. notify.<name>.http.headers map empty Header names and values Sent with every request, such as Authorization. A Content-Type here replaces application/json. notify.<name>.http.body string none, required A Go template The request body. See Send to another service for recipes.
